scope: Shared renderer device-context ownership and checked operation lifetimes are now Rust-owned. Text/path algorithms and buffers remain native.

preimplementation_inventory.scope: Source inventory plus directly observed cleanup lifecycle baseline for the next shared renderer device-context ownership port. Ownership is still C++.

acquire: Increment global signed refcount, including after failed CreateCompatibleDC
release: At zero call DeleteDC; ignore result; native g_hDC retains scalar
lifecycle.sharing: All renderer instances in one module use one global context. Native source warns to use only one RTS at a time.

borrowers: CMyFont constructor selects new font, queries metrics, restores previous selection
CText::GetTextInfo selects font, measures each UTF16 unit when spacing != 0 or wcslen prefix otherwise, restores on all paths
CText::CreatePath selects font; error exits restore; successful restore is ASSERT-only and omitted in Release
PathData uses caller HDC for begin/end and partial path acquisition
constraints: Use typed monotonic owner IDs; keep canonical device-context ownership in Rust. Native wrappers remain temporary.
Do not initialize context for every renderer or preserve it indefinitely after last owner.
Do not add successful-path SelectObject restoration to CText::CreatePath.
Return Windows handle scalars only under explicit scoped lifetime/serialization contract. No Rust pointer or mutable loan crosses FFI.
Reference CreateCompatibleDC failure, setup-call failures, nested renderer owners, release order, recreation and selected-font deletion before deciding error mapping.
Device contexts created with NULL can depend on creating-thread lifetime. Do not invent cross-thread ownership or move GDI calls to a worker.
Registry admission alone does not serialize full native text/path operations; whole-operation guard and host lock/reentry order remain to be established.

Canonical font construction re-enters DOCUMENTS; a whole text/path operation guard cannot simply hold that nonblocking registry admission across native calls. Establish separate operation/lifetime serialization and lock order.
The current font-create boundary rejects a null DC; failed-DC constructor lifecycle parity does not imply later text/font failure-path parity.
Keep explicit release at its original destructor point after Deinit and before remaining native member/base destruction. Preserve one unconditional DeleteDC attempt, including null.
preimplementation_inventory.next_probe: Nested document rectangle ownership is corrected at 03d78ffa and validated at ebd25901 (rust-document-rectangle-local-evidence.json). Promote the retained DC lifecycle fixture into the maintained runner/validator; extend DeleteDC failure and selected-font/text/path histories. Move shared canonical DC lifetime into Rust with typed owner IDs and an explicit whole-operation/thread-lifetime contract, then rerun lifecycle, font/GDI, exact rendering and hosts.

lifecycle_baseline.limits: This historical scoped GDI/status baseline does not compare nested document rectangle counts. That separate probe failed at 9105c8f5; the correction and current passing evidence are separately recorded in rust-document-rectangle-local-evidence.json.

observed_lifecycle_details: Nested owners share one DC; eight measured constructor/destructor phases have cumulative call counts 4,4,4,4,4,5,9,10. Last release deletes once; the next first owner recreates.
The four setup calls are CreateCompatibleDC(NULL), SetBkMode(1), SetTextColor(0x00ffffff), SetMapMode(1), in that order.
A scripted null creation still executes all three setup calls and counts nested owners. Last release still calls DeleteDC(NULL); do not use a generic non-null-only handle destructor.

In the retained null-creation trace, setup calls change last-error through 6,6,87; final DeleteDC(NULL) sets 6. Preserve API side effects rather than restoring caller errors around the complete operation.
Scripted individual SetBkMode, SetTextColor and SetMapMode failures do not stop subsequent setup or change sharing/release counts.
Two runs per role/architecture match raw return values, normalized handle generations, errno, last-error and separate x87/SSE flags at every call boundary and lifecycle phase.

ownership: A safe generic state machine issues non-rewinding checked owner and operation IDs. One native Context value is owned while any renderer owner remains.
First acquisition creates and configures the DC in the original call order; null creation remains an owned context and still receives setup calls.
Final release remains after renderer Deinit and before native member/base destruction. Context Drop attempts DeleteDC once, including null or failed deletion, without retry.
An operation token retains the context and excludes overlapping operations and owner changes. Its ABI packet contains only a Windows HDC scalar and checked token, never a Rust pointer.
lock_and_thread_contract: The shared recursive native adapter gate surrounds complete CText measurement/path calls, including font destruction. Nested font registry calls take that same gate recursively.
Short Rust DC admission ends before text/font calls. The retained operation token is separate from DOCUMENTS admission, avoiding a held registry loan during font creation.
Standalone FontIntern construction takes its own operation token; text methods pass the already active operation to the font adapter.
The creating thread must remain alive through final owner release. Calls run on the existing caller threads; no worker or cross-thread lifetime extension is introduced.

Busy/reentry and concurrent admission tests prove Rust exclusion/refusal behavior, not compatibility for arbitrary host reentry or concurrency. Native object lifetime and caches remain a separate migration boundary.
observed_quirks: Six lifecycle histories preserve call order, handle generations, return values, errno, last-error and independent x87/SSE status across nested owners, final release and recreation.

Create failure still executes all setup calls and DeleteDC(NULL). Setup failures do not stop subsequent calls. Scripted DeleteDC failure is ignored, and the next first owner creates a new DC. Probe-only cleanup occurs after observation.

Forty CText histories preserve raw path types/points, measurements, font-selection state and GDI call/status traces for spacing, embedded NUL, unpaired surrogate and empty inputs, with extent/begin/text/end failures.
Successful CreatePath leaves the font selected because the cleanup restoration is ASSERT-only. Tested checked failure exits restore it. Partial-path code retains its ignored failure behavior.
Measurement and spaced paths stop at the first NUL; unspaced path TextOut uses the CString length, including an embedded-NUL tail. These remain code-unit operations.
limits: Null constructor lifecycle parity does not establish later font/path behavior on a null DC; the existing font boundary safely refuses it. Font construction with no live renderer owner is also outside this comparison.
No claim for arbitrary allocator failures, GetPath negative/uninitialized results, selected-object teardown under arbitrary concurrency, or creating-thread termination.
C++ word/line/subtitle graphs, raw path buffers, host adapters and vendors remain in scope. No production default switched.
